content: If the patch does not adhere properly, you may secure it by applying medical tape or surgical bandages to the edges to ensure it stays in place. When it is time to remove the patch, gently peel it off. Fold the patch in half with the adhesive sides pressed together and dispose of it in a trash receptacle that is out of reach of children and pets. Do not reuse the patch. After removal, wash the application site and your hands thoroughly with soap and water. Mild redness at the application site may occur but should resolve within three days. Use this medication exactly as prescribed to achieve the maximum therapeutic benefit. Do not exceed the prescribed dosage. Constipation is a potential side effect. Remember, this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. This medication may increase serotonin levels and, in rare cases, lead to a serious condition known as serotonin syndrome or serotonin toxicity. The risk of this condition is heightened if you are taking other medications that also increase serotonin levels. Inform your doctor or pharmacist of all medications you are currently taking to avoid potential interactions. Severe allergic reactions to this medication are rare. However, this is not an exhaustive list of possible side effects. If you are in the United States, contact your doctor for medical advice regarding side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for similar guidance. Before using granisetron, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other complications. The medication may be affected by sunlight or make the application site more sensitive to sunlight. While wearing the patch, keep it covered (e.g., under clothing) to prevent exposure to sunlight or artificial UV light sources such as sunlamps. Avoid tanning booths. After removing the patch, keep the application site covered for an additional 10 days. If you are scheduled for an MRI, inform the testing personnel that you are using this patch, as some patches may contain metals that can cause serious burns during the procedure. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly necessary. It is unknown whether this medication passes into breast milk. Drug interactions may alter the effectiveness of your medications or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Maintain a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs as well as herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. The risk of serotonin syndrome or toxicity increases if you are also taking other drugs that elevate serotonin levels. Examples include street drugs like MDMA (ecstasy), St. John’s wort, and certain antidepressants such as SSRIs (e.g., fluoxetine, paroxetine) or SNRIs (e.g., duloxetine, venlafaxine). If someone overdoses on this medication patch, remove the patch if possible. For serious symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. If you miss a dose or fail to use the patch at the correct time before your scheduled chemotherapy appointment, inform your doctor promptly. Store the patch at room temperature, away from heat. Do not open the pouch until you are ready to use the patch. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
